title: Markdown in AI workflows
caption: A single format carrying three of the six context types: Knowledge, Instructions, and Memory.
prose: A plain text file with nothing mechanical underneath. What matters is how and when it is consumed: as knowledge, as instructions, as memory — and whether the agent pays for it on every turn or only when it reaches for it.

three-contexts.description: Markdown carries Knowledge, Instructions, and Memory with distinct lifecycle and retrieval costs.

retrieval-cost.description: What matters is whether the agent pays context tokens on every turn or retrieves on demand.

agentic-era.title: The agentic era
agentic-era.script: Before we start, I want to establish why markdown files matter so much in AI workflows. We're in the agentic era now — it isn't 2023 anymore. Agents aren't chatbots you copy-paste into. They read files on your machine, write files, call tools, search the web. Put those in a loop and they carry out real tasks, the way the new colleague you just onboarded would.

three-categories.title: Three categories of markdown
three-categories.script: And like that colleague, an agent needs the right information at the right time. That information lives in markdown — which is just a plain text file. Those files fall into three categories. Knowledge — what the agent looks up on demand, when the task calls for it. Instructions — skills: how to do a release, step by step, written once and called by name. And memory — not ChatGPT's memory, but a file the agent reads at the start of every single conversation. And if that file is stale, or wrong, the agent reads that wrong information every single time. Confidently, and silently — without you ever noticing.
